title: Enterprise Multi-Tenant RBAC Authorization Type Narrowing
businessContext: An enterprise ERP platform provides access to financial records. Different user roles (SuperAdmin, OrgAdmin, BillingAuditor, Viewer) have strictly segregated access to tenant resources. A security audit discovered that downstream handler code assumed all users have an `organizationId`, causing cross-tenant data leaks when SuperAdmins (who operate globally without an organizationId) called organization-scoped endpoints.
problemStatement: Design a custom type guard and discriminated context model for user sessions. Implement a type guard `isOrgScopedSession(session)` that narrows a general user session to an `OrgScopedUserSession` guaranteed to contain a non-nullable `tenantId` and valid organization permissions.
constraints: Type guards must use `session is OrgScopedUserSession` predicate.
Must enforce tenant isolation at compile time.
Must reject sessions with undefined or null tenantId.
candidateTasks: Implement `isOrgScopedSession` type guard correctly checking runtime fields.
Ensure the return type predicate `session is OrgScopedSession` narrows TypeScript type in if/else blocks.
Discuss how custom type predicates can be dangerous if the runtime logic does not match the type predicate declaration.
hints: A type guard must return a boolean and have return type `arg is TargetType`.
Check both role and that `tenantId !== null && typeof tenantId === "string"`.

testCases.name: Narrows org scoped session accurately
testCases.explanation: Allows scoped access with safe tenantId.

alternativeApproaches: Using Discriminated Unions on a "scope" tag (scope: "GLOBAL" | "ORG").
Using branded types for TenantId to prevent accidental substitution of user IDs for tenant IDs.
commonMistakes: Using type assertion "as OrgScopedSession" instead of a proper type guard.
Forgetting to check for empty strings or undefined in tenantId.
